# T005 — Patch backend Express HTTP dependency family

## Summary
On Node v24.21.0 / npm 11.19.0, patched Express 4 and body-parser 1 in the root workspace and standalone backend locks. The five targeted affected package names are absent from both fresh npm audits; all 35 existing tests pass. No application, ACS, or deployment code changed.

## Changes
- `backend/package.json`: raise the existing direct Express and body-parser lower bounds to `^4.22.3` and `^1.20.8`, respectively; both remain in their original major lines.
- `package-lock.json`: regenerated with `npm install --package-lock-only --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund --workspace backend 'express@^4.22.3' 'body-parser@^1.20.8'`. npm rehoisted backend HTTP packages from `backend/node_modules` to root `node_modules` and resolved their compatible children; no overrides.
- `backend/package-lock.json`: regenerated using `npm install --prefix backend --workspaces=false --package-lock-only --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund 'express@^4.22.3' 'body-parser@^1.20.8'`, then `npm update proxy-addr --prefix backend --workspaces=false --package-lock-only --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund` to refresh the existing `~2.0.7` transitive range to 2.0.8. npm also resolved compatible HTTP-chain `raw-body`, `side-channel` and other small dependencies.

## Decisions
Live advisory information checked 2026-10-20 against the GitHub Advisory Database (links in the table), both npm audit JSON files, and `npm view express@4.22.3 dependencies`. `npm explain express body-parser proxy-addr path-to-regexp qs --json` was run for the root graph and `--prefix backend` for the standalone graph: Express is backend direct; body-parser is backend direct **and** Express-owned; proxy-addr and path-to-regexp are Express-owned; qs is Express- and body-parser-owned. Express 4.22.3 declares `body-parser ~1.20.5`, `proxy-addr ~2.0.7`, `path-to-regexp ~0.1.13`, `qs ~6.16.0`; compatible npm resolution yields the fixed versions below without Express 5 or overrides. Baseline versions were the same in both locks. The `qs` row covers all four current audit GHSA entries; `express` is an aggregate affected parent rather than an additional independent advisory.

- From repository root, `CI=true TZ=UTC LANG=C.UTF-8`, `/opt/node/24/bin` first on `PATH`; exact full gates **after the last package edit**: `npm ci` passed; `npm run build --if-present` passed (three pre-existing CSS optimizer warnings); `npm test` passed **35/35**, zero failed, zero skipped (backend 15, frontend 20); `npm run lint --if-present` passed (five baseline warnings, zero errors).
- Additional exact gates: `npm ci --prefix backend` passed. `bash /shared/skills/dependency-vulnerability-remediation/scripts/scan-dependencies.sh --output-dir .modernization-scratch/scan .` exited **2** because unrelated advisories remain; **neither scan was incomplete**. Scanner uses native `npm audit --json` via npm 11.19.0; scan date 2026-10-20 UTC. Before: root 56 affected names (5 critical / 35 high / 13 moderate / 3 low), standalone backend 18 (2 / 10 / 6 / 0). After: root 51 (4 / 33 / 11 / 3), backend 13 (1 / 8 / 4 / 0). These are affected package-name counts, not individual advisories or additive across locks. Raw reports are local-only in `.modernization-scratch/scan/`.
- `git diff --check` passed. No HTTP-family target (`express`, `body-parser`, `proxy-addr`, `path-to-regexp`, `qs`) remains in either audit JSON.

## Follow-ups and risks
- Other audit findings remain open, **not accepted or clean**: root includes Azure identity/XML, speech, nodemon, Vite/Rollup, ESLint, Static Web Apps CLI, and shared UUID chains; backend still includes Azure/XML, speech, nodemon and UUID. Their planned owners are T006–T013. Root `cookie` low finding is owned by the Static Web Apps CLI (`cookie@0.5.0`, T011), not the patched Express HTTP copy (`cookie@0.7.x`).
- No live ACS integration or deployment verification was performed. Keep offline HTTP contracts and full gates in subsequent dependency tasks.
